competencies.text: Propose adaptation and mitigation strategies for local biodiversity.
Evaluate overpopulation effects from secondary sources.

days.title: Adaptation & Mitigation Strategies
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to distinguish between adaptation and mitigation, propose strategies for protecting local biodiversity, and evaluate how overpopulation affects ecosystems and climate.

🔑 Adaptation vs. Mitigation

TermMeaningFocusExample
AdaptationAdjusting to the effects of climate change that are already happeningManaging impactsBuilding seawalls; planting drought-resistant crops
MitigationReducing the causes of climate change — mainly GHG emissionsReducing emissionsUsing solar power; planting trees; reducing waste

Both are needed. We must adapt to what's already happening AND reduce future impacts.

🌱 Adaptation Strategies for the Philippines

StrategyHow It Helps
Mangrove restorationBuffers coastal communities from storm surges and sea-level rise; provides fish habitat
Climate-resilient cropsSalt-tolerant rice (e.g., NSIC Rc480), drought-resistant corn varieties
Rainwater harvestingCaptures rain during wet season for use during dry spells
Elevated homes and flood-proof infrastructureReduces damage from floods and storm surges
Early warning systemsPAGASA typhoon warnings; PHIVOLCS volcano/earthquake alerts
Diversified farmingReduces risk from crop failure — if one crop fails, others survive
Coral reef restorationCoral gardening; marine protected areas
Urban green spacesReduces heat island effect; absorbs CO₂ and stormwater

🌍 Mitigation Strategies

StrategyHow It Reduces Emissions
Renewable energySolar, wind, hydro, geothermal replace fossil fuels
ReforestationTrees absorb CO₂ from the atmosphere
Reduce, reuse, recycleLess waste = less methane from landfills
Public transportation & cyclingFewer cars = less CO₂
Energy-efficient appliancesLess electricity demand; lower emissions
Sustainable agricultureLess methane from livestock and rice paddies
Protect forests and wetlandsPreserves carbon sinks that store CO₂

🇵🇭 Philippine Climate Policies

  • Climate Change Act of 2009 (RA 9729): Created the Climate Change Commission (CCC).
  • Philippine Strategy for Sustainable Development: Aligns development with climate goals.
  • Renewable Energy Act (RA 9513): Promotes renewable energy development.
  • National Greening Program: Government reforestation initiative.
  • Extended Producer Responsibility Act (RA 11898): Makes companies responsible for plastic waste.

👥 Overpopulation and the Environment

The global population recently passed 8 billion. The Philippines has over 110 million people — one of the fastest-growing populations in Southeast Asia.

Effects of overpopulation on the environment and climate:

  • Increased resource demand: More food, water, energy needed → more pressure on ecosystems.
  • Deforestation: Forests cleared for housing, farming, and infrastructure.
  • More waste: More plastic, more methane from landfills.
  • Higher GHG emissions: More vehicles, factories, and electricity use.
  • Habitat loss: Coastal development destroys mangroves and reefs.
  • Water scarcity: More people competing for limited freshwater.
  • Food insecurity: More demand on fisheries and farmland.

🧠 What Can We Do?

Solutions to overpopulation's environmental impact:

  • Education, especially for girls — reduces family size and improves outcomes.
  • Access to family planning — empowers families to choose family size.
  • Urban planning — dense cities use less land and energy per person than sprawl.
  • Sustainable consumption — buying less, wasting less.
  • Renewable energy transition — decouple growth from emissions.

🌱 Biodiversity Protection in the Philippines

The Philippines is a megadiverse country — one of 17 countries that together contain 70% of the world's biodiversity. Threats include habitat loss, overfishing, pollution, and climate change.

Protection strategies:

  • Marine Protected Areas (MPAs): No-take zones let fish populations recover.
  • Protected terrestrial areas: NIPAS Act (RA 7586) creates national parks and wildlife sanctuaries.
  • Community-based conservation: Local communities manage resources — like the Tagbanwa in Palawan.
  • Wildlife protection laws: RA 9147 — Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act.

📌 Quick Check

  • What's the difference between adaptation and mitigation? (Answer: adaptation manages impacts; mitigation reduces causes)
  • Name one Philippine law related to climate. (Answer: RA 9729 Climate Change Act)
  • How does overpopulation affect the environment? (Answer: increases resource demand, deforestation, waste, and GHG emissions)

days.title: Match Game — Mitigation Actions
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each strategy, law, or concept to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Adjusting to the impacts of climate change — like building seawalls
Reducing the causes of climate change — like using solar power
Buffers coastal communities from storm surges and provides fish habitat
Captures rain during the wet season for dry-season use
Solar, wind, hydro, geothermal that replace fossil fuels
Philippine Climate Change Act of 2009 — created the CCC
Philippine Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act
No-take zone where fish populations recover

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Community Resilience
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🌊 A coastal barangay in Ilocos is being flooded every year by stronger storm surges. Which strategy is BEST for protecting the community?

choices.label: A) Build a sea wall only
B) Restore mangroves and elevate homes — natural barriers plus resilient infrastructure
C) Move the entire barangay inland
D) Ignore it — it will get better on its own

scenario.text: 🌾 A rice farmer in Nueva Ecija is worried about future droughts. What adaptation strategy should they adopt?

choices.label: A) Plant drought-resistant rice varieties and harvest rainwater
B) Plant more water-demanding crops
C) Use more fertilizer
D) Farm only during the rainy season

scenario.text: 🏙️ Metro Manila is experiencing extreme heat and flooding. Which combination of strategies BEST reduces both problems?

choices.label: A) Plant urban trees and create green spaces — reduces heat and absorbs stormwater
B) Build more parking lots
C) Cut down all trees to improve visibility
D) Increase private car use

scenario.text: 👥 A growing city doubles in population in 20 years. What environmental effects are likely?

choices.label: A) More waste, more emissions, more pressure on water and food supplies, and loss of surrounding forests
B) Cleaner air and water
C) Fewer vehicles and factories
D) No changes to the environment

scenario.text: 🐠 A coastal community wants to restore fish populations. Which strategy is BEST?

choices.label: A) Establish a Marine Protected Area (no-take zone) and enforce fishing limits
B) Increase fishing intensity
C) Introduce invasive fish species
D) Build a resort over the reef

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Resilience Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Resilience Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. This is your final formative check before the Term Exam.

escape.text: What is the difference between adaptation and mitigation?

choices.label: A) Adaptation adjusts to climate impacts; mitigation reduces the causes of climate change
B) Adaptation reduces emissions; mitigation adjusts to impacts
C) They are the same thing
D) Both only apply to farming

escape.text: Which strategy is an example of MITIGATION?

choices.label: A) Switching to solar energy to reduce fossil fuel use
B) Building a sea wall
C) Planting drought-resistant crops
D) Elevating homes above flood level

escape.text: Which strategy is an example of ADAPTATION?

choices.label: A) Restoring mangroves to buffer storm surges
B) Installing solar panels
C) Reducing plastic use
D) Riding a bicycle instead of driving

escape.text: Which Philippine law created the Climate Change Commission?

choices.label: A) RA 9729 (Climate Change Act of 2009)

escape.text: How does overpopulation affect the environment?

choices.label: A) It increases resource demand, deforestation, waste, and greenhouse gas emissions
B) It reduces pollution
C) It has no environmental impact
D) It only affects cities, not farms

escape.text: Which of the following BEST protects Philippine biodiversity?

choices.label: A) Establishing Marine Protected Areas and enforcing wildlife laws like RA 9147
B) Increasing fishing intensity
C) Converting forests to farmland
D) Importing more exotic species
